questions.question: Why is plain self-attention unable to tell that two differently ordered sentences mean different things?
options: It always deletes repeated tokens
It is permutation-invariant unless position information is added
It only works on fixed-length sequences
It requires a recurrent hidden state to encode meaning
questions.explanation: The lesson says attention is order-blind: shuffling the rows of the input just shuffles the outputs the same way. Without an added positional signal, the mechanism itself has no notion of sequence order.

questions.question: What kind of extra information must a positional method provide to attention?
options: The exact gradient at each layer
The optimizer state for each token
Some signal about token position or relative distance
A larger vocabulary embedding table
questions.explanation: All three approaches in the lesson exist to restore order information. They do it differently, but each injects some notion of where tokens are or how far apart they are.

questions.question: In the original sinusoidal approach, where is the positional signal inserted?
options: Added to token embeddings before the first attention layer
Added only to the output logits
Used only inside the feed-forward network
Stored in the optimizer instead of the model
questions.explanation: The sinusoidal method precomputes a positional matrix and adds it directly to the embeddings. The lesson explicitly writes X' = X + PE[:N] before attention begins.

questions.question: What is the key effect of applying RoPE to queries and keys?
options: It makes attention scores depend only on relative distance between positions
It removes the need for softmax
It forces all heads to share the same projection matrix
It turns attention into a convolution
questions.explanation: RoPE rotates Q and K by position-dependent angles, but the resulting dot product depends on m - n rather than on the absolute positions alone. That is why the lesson describes RoPE as encoding relative position directly inside the attention score.

questions.question: How does ALiBi encode position?
options: By appending a learned position token to the sequence
By rotating embeddings with sinusoids
By adding a head-specific linear distance penalty to attention scores
By masking out every token more than one step away
questions.explanation: ALiBi does not modify embeddings at all in this lesson's formulation. Instead, it subtracts m_h · |i - j| from attention scores, which biases heads toward closer tokens while still allowing long-context extrapolation.
